sections.label: CPF transfer and Act changes
sections.summary: The changes allow more CPF members to transfer to parents and grandparents, update the Retirement Sum exemption payout benchmark, and clarify CPF Act administration.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: First, it will allow more CPF members to make CPF transfers to their parents and grandparents.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Second, it will update the payout benchmark for Retirement Sum exemption.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Third, it will clarify and streamline the administration of some parts of the CPF Act.

sections.label: CPF transfers below age 55
sections.summary: A member below 55 may transfer OA savings above the Basic Retirement Sum to parents and grandparents if remaining savings meet the prevailing BRS and FRS.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: A member below the age of 55 will be able to transfer part of his OA savings above the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) to his parents and grandparents if he has sufficient OA and SA savings to meet the prevailing BRS, which together with a property charge, are sufficient to meet the prevailing FRS.

sections.label: More members eligible for transfers
sections.summary: About 20% of CPF members aged 30 to 70 meet current transfer thresholds, and the amendment raises eligibility to 30%.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: About 20% of CPF members aged 30 to 70 meet the current thresholds to make transfers to their parents and grandparents.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: With the amendment, 30% of CPF members will be eligible.

sections.label: Lower threshold for CPF top-ups
sections.summary: A lower threshold lets members top up their parents' and grandparents' CPF accounts for their retirement needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The move to implement a lower threshold to allow members to make CPF transfers to top up their parents' and grandparents' CPF accounts provides members the option to build up their parents' or grandparents' CPF accounts for their retirement needs.

sections.label: Elderly healthcare costs projection
sections.summary: An MMC Asia Pacific Risk Center report projects Singapore's total elderly healthcare costs to rise tenfold over 15 years to US$49 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Based on a report by Marsh & McLennan Companies' (MMC's) Asia Pacific Risk Center, the total healthcare costs of the elderly in Singapore are projected to rise tenfold over the next 15 years to US$49 billion annually.

sections.label: Median resident age rise
sections.summary: The median age of the resident population rose from 34 years in 2000 to 40.5 years in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The median age of the resident population rose from 34 years in 2000 to 40.5 years in 2017.

sections.label: Returning top-ups after death
sections.summary: Asks whether top-up balances can return to the contributor's CPF with interest when the parent or grandparent dies, or whether the CPF nomination prevails.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Sixth, would the Minister consider allowing the balance of top-ups in the parent's or grandparent's accounts to be returned to the contributing member’s CPF account with accrued interest when the parent or grandparent whom he has contributed to passes away or that the CPF nomination still prevails?

sections.label: Annuity take-up and CPF advice
sections.summary: Asks the take-up rate for the option and whether CPF Board advises members choosing a personal annuity on differences between institution annuities and CPF schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share the take-up rate for this option?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In the event where the member decides to procure a personal annuity to be exempted from setting aside the Retirement Sum in his CPF account, does CPF Board offer advisory services to such members to assist them in assessing the difference between the annuities offered by the financial institutions and CPF schemes or is the advising left solely in the hands of the financial planner from the financial institution?

sections.label: Tax relief for cash top-ups
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will highlight the tax relief option of withdrawing CPF excess first then doing a cash top-up, and whether the amendment becomes a white elephant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: By doing so, some of these members may get to enjoy additional tax relief of up to $7,000 per calendar year, which they would not enjoy if they were to subscribe to the proposed amendment, which is to do a top-up via CPF transfer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry highlight this tax relief option to the members so that they can make an informed choice, that is, they could be better off withdrawing the excess amount standing in their CPF accounts first, then follow up with a cash top-up to the CPF accounts of their loved ones later, so as to enjoy some tax relief in the process?

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Would the latest amendment to section 18 become a white elephant since qualified members are better off doing the cash top-up option?

sections.label: Informed retirement planning choices
sections.summary: Hopes the Ministry helps CPF members make informed retirement adequacy choices and notes amendments lower the threshold for transfers to parents and grandparents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Beyond providing options to the CPF system, I hope the Ministry can help CPF members make informed choices towards planning for their own retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened to note that the amendments to the CPF Act will improve the retirement adequacy of older CPF members by lowering the threshold for CPF members to make transfers to their parents and grandparents.

sections.label: Exclusion of parents-in-law
sections.summary: Asks why the amendments are not extended to parents-in-law and grandparents-in-law, in line with filial piety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In line with the core value of filial piety, can the Minister clarify why the amendments will not be extended to parents-in-law and grandparents-in-law?

sections.label: Tax reliefs for family transfers
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government will consider tax reliefs for CPF transfers to parents, parents-in-law, grandparents, grandparents-in-law, siblings and spouses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, to further encourage familial support within the CPF framework, will the Government consider tax reliefs for CPF transfers to parents, parents-in-law, grandparents, grandparents-in-law, siblings and spouses?

sections.label: CPF members meeting BRS
sections.summary: In 2013, about six in 10 active CPF members who turned age 55 met their cohort BRS.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In 2013, about six in 10 active CPF members who turned age 55 met their cohort BRS.

sections.label: Eligible members increase expected
sections.summary: The speaker expects the number of eligible members to increase by 340,000.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Nonetheless, as I have shared in my earlier speech, we expect that the number of eligible members will increase by 340,000.

sections.label: Refund of transferred CPF monies
sections.summary: Transferred CPF monies not streamed out as payouts before the recipient's demise would be refunded to the giver's CPF accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To safeguard the giver's retirement adequacy, all the transferred CPF monies that had not been streamed out as CPF payouts to the recipient before the recipient’s demise would be refunded to the giver’s CPF accounts.

sections.label: CPF contributions tax treatment
sections.summary: CPF contributions are already tax deductible and interest earned on the contributions are not taxable.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Currently, CPF contributions are already tax deductible and interest earned on the contributions are not taxable.

sections.label: Higher interest via transfers
sections.summary: Members can enjoy higher interest by transferring monies from their OA to their loved ones' SA or RA.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, members can enjoy higher interest by transferring monies from their OA, which earns up to 3.5%, to their loved ones’ SA or RA, which earns up to 6%.

sections.label: CPF consultation at age 54
sections.summary: When a member turns 54, CPF Board will invite them to a one-on-one consultation explaining CPF options and decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: When a member turns 54, CPF Board will invite them to a one-on-one, face-to-face, consultation where CPF Board staff will explain the CPF options, including the impact on reliefs, for example, as well as the decisions that they can make.
